skill.name: orchestrating-parallel-agents
skill.description: Coordinates multiple AI coding agents working on related GitHub issues through git worktrees, wave planning, monitoring, PR merging, and cleanup.
skill.summary: Coordinate parallel coding agents with issue waves, git worktrees, monitoring, PR handling, and cleanup.
skill.author: 4eyedengineer

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline backticks. Real risk remains where the skill recommends pre-approved git write permissions, background agent launches, and git or GitHub commands that push, merge, force-push, or delete branches. No prompt injection or covert exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict Bash allow rules to exact worktrees and commands, and require explicit approval for push and merge steps.
Add guidance for small waves, trusted issue text, concurrency limits, and stopping background processes before continuing.
Add preflight checks for status, branch name, remote target, tests, and reviewed diffs before push, merge, force-push, or branch deletion.

semantic_findings.title: Unattended Git Write Permissions
semantic_findings.description: The permissions section tells users to allow Bash git add, commit, and push rules for non-interactive mode. This can let agents alter repository state without per-command confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text directly recommends pre-approved git write permissions in the only analyzed file. The security impact is clear because the allowed commands change repository state.

semantic_findings.title: Parallel Background Agent Execution
semantic_findings.description: The spawn section starts several Claude processes in the background for issue IDs. Parallel unattended execution can multiply failures when issue prompts are unclear or hostile.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The bash loop shows concurrent background agent execution. The risk depends on operator controls, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Repository State Changes
semantic_findings.description: The workflow guides users through push, PR creation, PR merge, rebase, and force-push recovery commands. These operations can publish or rewrite repository history without careful review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands are explicit git and GitHub CLI operations that affect remote branches or pull requests. Their impact is operational rather than hidden or malicious.

content.value_statement: Coordinating several coding agents can create merge conflicts, permission gaps, and lost work. This skill gives a wave-based workflow for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code teams.
actual_capabilities: Breaks large features into small, file-scoped GitHub issues.
Organizes independent and dependent work into execution waves.
Shows how to prepare non-interactive Claude CLI runs.
Provides commands for spawning agents and collecting logs.
Covers monitoring, PR handling, rebase recovery, and cleanup.
Highlights review points for conflicts and off-scope work.
limitations: Assumes GitHub, git worktrees, GitHub CLI, and Claude CLI are available.
Does not create issues, worktrees, or pull requests by itself.
Requires human review before merging or force pushing branches.
Can increase risk when permissions are too broad.

use_cases.title: Plan Multi-Issue Feature Work
use_cases.description: Split one large feature into isolated issues and execution waves before assigning agents.

use_cases.title: Run Concurrent Coding Agents
use_cases.description: Launch several agents for independent GitHub issues while keeping logs and progress visible.

use_cases.title: Recover and Merge Agent PRs
use_cases.description: Handle straggler branches, merge conflicts, rebase steps, and worktree cleanup after agent runs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Parallel Wave
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to split my feature into three small GitHub issues. Group them into safe waves and list review checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Agent-Ready Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to turn my feature notes into agent-ready issues with files to modify, acceptance criteria, and merge order.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Safe Agent Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a parallel Claude CLI run. Include wave order, logging names, permission checks, and manual stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Recover Conflicted Agent Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to recover a conflicted agent branch after another PR merged. Include rebase checks, review gates, and cleanup steps.

output_examples.input: I need to split a dashboard redesign across agents.
output: A wave plan with independent backend and frontend issues.
Issue briefs with file targets, acceptance criteria, and merge order.
A review checklist for PR merge and worktree cleanup.

output_examples.input: Three agents finished, but one pull request conflicts after merge.
output_examples.output: A recovery plan that rebases the affected worktree, lists manual conflict checks, and confirms the branch before force pushing.

output_examples.input: I want to run agents without interactive approvals.
output: A permission review plan for exact worktree paths.
A warning about push and merge approvals.
A monitoring checklist for background agent logs.

best_practices: Keep each issue small, file-scoped, and testable.
Place same-file changes in separate waves or one agent assignment.
Review diffs, tests, permissions, and branch targets before repository changes.
anti_patterns: Do not grant broad Bash permissions for unknown worktrees.
Do not run many agents against overlapping files in one wave.
Do not merge, force push, or delete branches without reviewing state.

faq.question: What does this skill help me coordinate?
faq.answer: It helps coordinate multiple coding agents working on related GitHub issues with git worktrees and staged waves.

faq.question: Does it run agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and example commands that a user must review and run.

faq.question: Which tools does it assume?
faq.answer: It assumes git worktrees, GitHub CLI, and a Claude CLI workflow. Other agent CLIs need equivalent commands.

faq.question: How should I reduce merge conflicts?
faq.answer: Keep issues small, avoid same-file edits in one wave, and merge same-file pull requests sequentially.

faq.question: Is non-interactive mode safe?
faq.answer: It can be useful, but only with narrow permissions, trusted prompts, and human review before push or merge steps.

faq.question: What should I do when an agent gets stuck?
faq.answer: Inspect the worktree and logs, finish safe changes manually, or reject the branch and clarify the issue.
